claims.claim: Apply SP 800-53 Rev 5 programme-level families: planning, program management, risk assessment, acquisition, supply chain, contingency, incident response, PII.
claims.evidence_quote: Planning ; Program Management ; Personnel Security ; PII Processing and Transparency ; Risk Assessment ; System and Services Acquisition
claims.note: Scope description: all eight family areas it names appear by full name in the Control Families list of the SP 800-53 Rev. 5 page - the quote shows five, and Contingency Planning, Incident Response and Supply Chain Risk Management appear in the same list - though the page states no 'programme-level' grouping.

claims.claim: programme-level families, including those new in Rev 5.
claims.note: No fetched page states that any family is new in Rev 5 or uses the term 'programme-level'; the 800-53 page's only 'new' statement is its 2025 planning note listing release-5.2.0 control changes (SA-15(13), SA-24, SI-02(07)).

claims.claim: Rev 5 has 20 families: AC AT AU CA CM CP IA IR MA MP PE PL PM PS PT RA SA SC SI SR.
claims.note: The 800-53 Rev. 5 page's Control Families section lists exactly 20 families by full name in the same order as these acronyms, and the list's HTML container carries data-total='20', but the page text never states the count and the two-letter identifiers appear on none of the three fetched pages.

claims.claim: New in Rev 5: PT (PII processing and transparency) and SR (supply chain risk management).
claims.note: Both families appear by full name in the 800-53 page's Control Families list, so the parenthetical expansions match, but no fetched page says either family was added in Rev 5; the r4-to-r5 changes are only in a linked xlsx that is neither a listed source nor page text.

claims.claim: PM controls are organisation-wide, not baseline-assigned.
claims.note: No fetched page says anything about the PM family's scope or baseline assignment; the abstract's 'controls are flexible and customizable and implemented as part of an organization-wide process to manage risk' is about controls generally, and 800-37's keyword 'control baseline' carries no PM statement.

claims.claim: RA-3 risk assessment, RA-5 vulnerability monitoring.
claims.note: 'RA-3' and 'RA-5' appear on none of the three fetched pages; 'Risk Assessment' appears only as a family name on the 800-53 page, and 'vulnerability' only in the site footer's Vulnerability Disclosure link.

claims.claim: SA-11 developer testing. SR-3 supply chain controls.
claims.note: 'SA-11', 'SR-3', 'developer' and 'testing' appear on none of the three fetched pages; 'System and Services Acquisition' and 'Supply Chain Risk Management' appear only as family names.

claims.claim: CP-2 contingency plan, CP-9 backup. IR-4 incident handling.
claims.note: 'CP-2', 'CP-9', 'backup' and 'incident handling' appear nowhere; 'Contingency Planning' and 'Incident Response' appear only as family names, and 'IR-04' appears once, only in the 2025 planning note's list of controls updated in release 5.2.0.

claims.claim: List the 20 family identifiers from memory, then verify against the catalog.
claims.note: Self-check line: no fetched page states a family count in its text; the 800-53 page lists 20 families by full name and its HTML carries data-total='20', but no sentence gives the number or the identifiers.

coverage: I took the frontmatter description, the Goal line, both body bullets - the 20-family count with its 20 two-letter acronyms, the new-in-Rev-5 PT and SR families, the PM organisation-wide/not-baseline-assigned behaviour, and the RA-3, RA-5, SA-11, SR-3, CP-2, CP-9 and IR-4 control statements - and the self-check line, covering every number, identifier and behaviour in the file, and checked each against all three listed sources, fetched and read today (all HTTP 200 via the attest fetcher); the H1 acronym list was treated as the topic title subsumed by the description and 20-family claims.
suggested_edits: Nothing is contradicted, but only the description's family scope is confirmed: the SP 800-53 Rev. 5 landing page lists all 20 control families by full name (its HTML list container even carries data-total='20'), yet its text never states the count, never uses two-letter identifiers, never says PT and SR are new in Rev 5, and has no control-level content - RA-3, RA-5, SA-11, SR-3, CP-2, CP-9 and IR-4 appear nowhere (IR-04 only in a 2025 planning-note change list) - and nothing on PM controls being organisation-wide rather than baseline-assigned; the cyberframework and SP 800-37 pages add nothing on any claim. A fix PR should bump version and cite sources that state these facts - the SP 800-53 Rev 5 document itself (nvlpubs PDF or the CPRT catalog) for the 20 families, their acronyms and control titles, the r4-to-r5 comparison workbook linked from the page for what is new in Rev 5, and SP 800-53B for which controls are baseline-assigned - or trim the skill to what the landing pages support.
